new_candidates.body:
## Desired behavior
Add a simulated marine radar sensor for Gazebo Harmonic with ROS 2 support, designed to be mounted on a USV (unmanned surface vehicle). Most Gazebo sensor setups are built around land and aerial robots, so marine-specific sensors such as radar are largely missing. A radar plugin that publishes standard ROS 2 messages would let users test USV perception, collision avoidance, and sensor fusion in simulation without hardware.

The sensor should expose configurable parameters for:
- Maximum range, beam geometry, and update rate
- Noise and clutter assumptions
- Mounting pose on the vessel

## Alternatives considered
- Using existing LiDAR or camera sensors as stand-ins for radar. These do not reproduce radar's range, resolution, or noise characteristics.
- Writing one-off radar models inside individual projects. This duplicates effort and does not give the community a shared, documented implementation.
- Reusing marine simulation packages such as Stonefish or the UUV Simulator. I have not yet confirmed whether they provide a radar sensor, so this comparison is still open.

## Implementation suggestion
- Implement as a Gazebo sensor plugin that publishes ROS 2 messages.
- Document the model's range, beam, noise, and clutter parameters so users can judge whether it fits their use case.
- Provide a sample world, launch file, and a short README showing a radar mounted on a USV.
- Release under a permissive license.
- If possible, validate the simulated output against a small recording from a real radar.

## Additional context
I am developing this as part of my own work and would welcome feedback on the model design and on whether it would be useful to others.
new_candidates.title: Marine Radar for Gazebo
